name: Optimus
priceNote: No list price. Musk said in Oct 2024 that at scale it could cost $20,000-$30,000; that is a long-term target, not a quote.

The Gen 3 (V3) design was promised for Q1 2026 and has slipped several times; as of late September 2026 it has not been formally unveiled. There is no price and no way to order one.

summary: Isaac 1 is a wheeled, fabric-covered home robot with two arms and simple two-finger grippers. Its torso adjusts from 0.9 m to 1.75 m, and it is built to fold laundry, make beds and tidy up. name: G1
priceNote: From $13,500 on Unitree's own store (base model, no SDK). US dealers quote about $16,000 and up; the EDU version with SDK and hands is quote-only.
compute: 8-core CPU; optional NVIDIA Jetson Orin module on EDU
releaseNote: Announced May 2024; shipping to research and business buyers since late 2024
summary: A 1.32 m, 35 kg research humanoid and the most widely sold humanoid in the world. It is the robot most labs buy to try humanoid control. Base units have no dexterous hands (the 7-DOF Dex3-1 hand is an EDU option), and it is not a household helper. Known Bluetooth and telemetry security problems are documented.

autonomy.note: Ships with factory locomotion controllers and a remote. Useful task behavior comes from the buyer's own code or teleoperation; Unitree does not sell autonomous chores.

legal.fccNote: FCC ID 2A5PE-YUSHU008 (grantee Hangzhou Yushu Technology), reported granted 2025-03-03. Authorized before the 2026-07-28 Covered List action, so sales and use can continue.
legal.security: UniPwn (Sept 2025): the BLE Wi-Fi setup accepts injected commands and every unit shares one hardcoded AES key, so anyone in Bluetooth range can get root. It can spread robot to robot (CVE-2025-35027, also affects Go2, H1 and B2). Alias Robotics researchers also reported the G1 sending telemetry to servers in China about every 5 minutes. The FCC's national-security determination cites UniPwn.

legal.security: UniPwn (Sept 2025): hard-coded BLE keys (CVE-2025-60250) plus Wi-Fi setup command injection (CVE-2025-35027) give root over Bluetooth and can spread robot to robot; affects Go2, G1, H1, B2. CVE-2026-27509 (Feb 2026, CVSS 8.5): unauthenticated DDS topic lets a nearby attacker run code as root on Go2 firmware 1.1.7-1.1.11. The older Go1 shipped with an undocumented CloudSail remote-access tunnel (CVE-2025-2894).

name: SO-101
priceNote: Hugging Face estimates about $100-$130 for one arm with printed parts and motors. A leader + follower pair is about $230 in parts (RobotStudio BOM); Seeed's dual-arm motor kit is $220-$240 without printed parts, and assembled pairs run up to about $500.
compute: None on board; runs from a USB-connected PC or NVIDIA Jetson via LeRobot
releaseNote: Open-source design released April 2025; kits sold by several vendors
summary: A 3D-printable, six-motor desktop arm built for the LeRobot framework, usually sold as a pair: you move a leader arm by hand and the follower copies it, recording data to train a policy. It is the cheapest serious way to try robot learning at home. The gripper is simple and payload is small, so expect pick-and-place demos, not chores.

autonomy.note: Designed around leader-follower teleoperation for data collection; can then run learned policies (e.g. ACT, SmolVLA) autonomously on narrow tasks.

legal.fccNote: A stationary, tethered arm with no radio; outside the FCC 'advanced robotic device' definition, which covers mobile robots only.

name: LeKiwi
priceNote: Full build about $482 (12V) or $499 (5V) in US parts per the project BOM, including the SO-101 arm and Raspberry Pi 5. Seeed sells the base-only kit for $179 without arm, Pi or cameras.
compute: Raspberry Pi 5 (streams to a laptop for policy inference)
releaseNote: Open-source design published February 2025; DIY and assembled kits sold by several vendors
summary: An SO-101 arm on a three-wheel omnidirectional base, making the cheapest open-source mobile manipulator for LeRobot. You drive it with a keyboard and a leader arm to record demonstrations, then train policies on the data. It is a learning platform, top speed 0.4 m/s, not a finished home helper.

autonomy.note: Teleoperated by leader arm plus keyboard for data collection; learned policies can run autonomously on simple tasks.

legal.fccNote: A self-assembled open-source build with no whole-robot FCC authorization; radios are in off-the-shelf modules (Raspberry Pi). The FCC rule's treatment of hobbyist kits is not addressed; weight not published, so the 4.4 lb threshold is unverified.

name: B2
priceNote: Listed at $100,000 on Unitree's US store; resellers quote roughly $77,000-$95,000 for base and lidar builds, and far more fully configured.
compute: Intel Core i5 standard; optional Intel Core i7 or NVIDIA Orin NX
releaseNote: Launched November 2023 for industrial inspection and load carrying
summary: Unitree's heavy industrial quadruped, an IP67 robot aimed at the same inspection jobs as Spot at a lower list price. It carries over 40 kg while walking and runs more than five hours unloaded. It shares firmware security flaws with the Go2 and is not a consumer product.

autonomy.note: Remote-controlled or run on programmed inspection routes; autonomy depends on optional lidar and compute modules.

legal.fccNote: FCC ID 2A5PE-YUSHU006 (quadruped robot, granted 2023-10-16 per FCC ID listings). Authorized before 2026-07-28; Unitree says B2 holds FCC authorization and may continue to be sold.
legal.security: Affected by UniPwn (Sept 2025): hard-coded BLE keys (CVE-2025-60250) and Wi-Fi setup command injection (CVE-2025-35027) allow root takeover over Bluetooth.

name: Pupper v3
priceNote: The project says you can build Pupper v3 yourself for about $2,000. Reseller AIFITLAB sells a parts kit from $1,450 that excludes printed parts, battery and controller.
compute: Raspberry Pi 5 (8 GB) with M.2 slot for an AI accelerator
releaseNote: Open-source build; v3 is the platform for Stanford's CS 123 course
summary: An open-source, 3 kg robot dog with brushless motors, a fisheye camera, a screen face and a microphone, designed to teach motor control and reinforcement learning. Stanford's CS 123 students build one from a starter kit each spring. It is a teaching and research platform you assemble yourself, not a finished pet.

autonomy.note: Walks under gamepad control; students add learned locomotion, object tracking and voice responses.

legal.fccNote: A self-built open-source design with no whole-robot FCC authorization; radios are in the Raspberry Pi. At 3 kg it exceeds the 2 kg mobile-robot threshold, but the July 2026 rule does not address hobbyist kits and it is designed in the US.
